records.title: Detecting nuclear weapons in space
records.description: An article in Nature proposes a method for detecting nuclear weapons on satellites.

records.title: Hamiltonians for action without reaction
records.description: An article in Nature Physics demonstrates how to construct Hamiltonians that generate the dynamics of systems with non-reciprocal interactions under a constraint.

records.title: Retrieving the amplitude and phase of ultrafast modulations with GRUMPY FROG
records.description: Anthony Harwood introduces GRUMPY FROG, an optical technique that retrieves the amplitude and phase of ultrafast material modulations from standard pump–probe measurements.

records.title: Neutrinos and the origins of particle dark matter
records.description: Although the search for a dark matter particle has so far produced only null results, its principles continue to drive dark matter research. This Perspective discusses how the dark matter particle concept evolved and reflects on how this history continues to shape the search for dark matter today.

records.title: Sensing electron vortices with nanomechanics
records.description: An article in Physical Review Letters introduces a nanomechanical probe of electron hydrodynamics.

records.title: Thin-film lithium niobate photonics for quantum technologies
records.description: Thin-film lithium niobate offers a promising platform for integrated photonic applications. This Perspective discusses how its material and optical properties can solve bottlenecks in quantum technologies.

records.title: Careers in physics
records.description: Careers rarely come with a map. Our new Careers in physics series provides advice, perspectives and lived experiences to help physicists navigate an increasingly varied professional landscape.

records.title: From curiosity to impact
records.description: Lan Yang, professor at Washington University in St. Louis and co-founder of DeepSight Technology, shares her experience of pursuing meaningful results in different ways.

records.title: Leading a research group with curiosity and collaboration
records.description: Sylvain Gigan, professor at Sorbonne University and deputy director of Laboratoire Kastler-Brossel in Paris, explains how collaboration is the key to successful research.

records.title: An unexpected journey to nanophotonics
records.description: Abdoulaye Ndao, Associate Professor at the University of California San Diego, recounts how one email changed the trajectory of his career.

records.title: The 3D Universe in a book
records.description: Brian May and Derek Ward-Thompson discuss the dynamical world of modern astronomy, which is beautifully captured in their stereoscopic book, Islands in Infinity .

records.title: Carnot’s cycle in the making of thermodynamics
records.description: Starting from the problem of steam engines, Sadi Carnot’s ideal cycle became a way to compare real processes with physical limits. Physicist and historian of the physical and mathematical sciences Raffaele Pisano traces how machines, diagrams, later theoretical reinterpretation and archival evidence turned an engineering problem into a durable thermodynamic law.

records.title: Taking the temperature of a cancer cell
records.description: An article in Science Advances introduces a method for measuring the temperature inside living cells.

records.title: Tipping points in complex ecological systems
records.description: Tipping points are sudden transitions in complex nonlinear systems that present unique challenges for theory and empirical work. This Review emphasizes the role of timescales, spatial complexity and complexity of ecological interactions, outlining theoretical progress that applies to these systems and providing empirical examples.

records.title: Levitodynamics beyond the ground state of motion
records.description: Ground-state cooling of levitated particles has brought the field of levitodynamics into the quantum regime, but the next steps are less clear. This Perspective highlights advances and challenges in two key frontiers — precision sensing and generation of non-classical states of motion.

records.title: Getting above the clouds
records.description: Paul Bate has gone from particle physics to Number 10 Downing Street to the UK Space Agency and beyond. Throughout, he has delivered on big ideas by recognizing expertise in others.

records.title: Meeting report: supermassive black holes and blue notes
records.description: To understand the physics of supermassive black holes across cosmic time, researchers with a variety of backgrounds convened in Montréal, Canada, to find synergies across multiple length scales, wavelengths and methodologies.

records.title: Excitonic order in quantum materials
records.description: Excitonic insulators are many-body states in which electron–hole pairing drives insulating behaviour with coherent condensate properties. This Review examines diverse experimental fingerprints of the excitonic state and proposes strategies to disentangle excitonic order from competing phases.

records.title: How scientists can engage with policymakers
records.description: As research agendas are increasingly set by governments, engaging with policymakers is becoming an important part of practicing and shaping science. Jess Wade explains how to get started.

records.title: Researchers need schools as much as schools need researchers
records.description: Research-in-schools programmes are known to positively impact students, but what of their impact on researchers? Evidence from Orbyts suggests they provide a powerful form of professional development for scientists and STEM professionals.

records.title: Nobel 2006: making cosmology a precision science
records.description: 20 years ago, the Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to John C. Mather and George F. Smoot.

records.title: Nobel 1946: high pressure physics
records.description: 80 years ago, the Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Percy Williams Bridgman.

records.title: Nobel 1966: atomic collaboration
records.description: 60 years ago, the 1966 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Alfred Kastler.

records.title: Scaling strategies for photonic neural networks
records.description: Photonic neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but scaling them remains challenging by architecture-dependent trade-offs. This Review surveys spatial, temporal, spectral and informational scaling strategies across leading architectures, emphasizing insights into hybrid design and the future development of large-scale photonic computing.

records.title: Interplay of topology and reversible associations in multi-responsive macromolecular networks
records.description: This Review presents a framework to understand and exploit the rheology of polymeric networks at different length and time scales, by critically comparing the linear and nonlinear response of branched macromolecules with that of associating networks possessing different types of bonds.

records.title: Physics students learn the ropes
records.description: Could this be the world’s only physics course with a swimming prerequisite?

records.title: Optical information security
records.description: Advances in quantum technology jeopardize current cryptography protocols. This review surveys optical information security across classical, quantum and hybrid schemes, sketching a pathway to secure photonic systems for the post-quantum era.

records.title: Estimating optical frequency comb linewidths using the β -separation line
records.description: Maximilian Prinz explains a technique to estimate the optical linewidth of a frequency comb from phase-noise measurements.

records.title: Self-organizing memristive networks as physical learning systems
records.description: Self-organizing memristive networks combine adaptive nanoscale transport, network connectivity and physical plasticity to enable learning directly in hardware. Their emergent dynamics, including criticality, memory and self-organization, offer a promising route towards energy-efficient neuromorphic computing and embedded physical intelligence.

records.title: Proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometry for tracking trace-level volatile organic compounds
records.description: Olivier Durif describes how mass spectroscopy can help to detect organic gases at trace levels.

records.title: Microscale droplets for mechanical measurement and mechanotransduction in artificial and living systems
records.description: Microscale droplets can sense and exert mechanical forces in biological environments. This Review examines the physical principles and engineering of liquid and hydrogel droplets as biointerfaces for measuring cellular mechanics and transducing mechanical cues into biochemical and electrical outputs.

records.title: Science is a process not a product
records.description: With an increasing number of startups coming out of universities, we examine the differences and similarities between academic and industrial research.

records.title: Four faces of information in natural systems
records.description: This Perspective proposes a pluralistic understanding of ‘information’ that reflects how this notion is used in natural sciences today. It distinguishes engineering, statistical, thermodynamic and ontological faces of information, each with distinctive affordances and restrictions.

records.title: Topological pair density waves in kagome superconductors
records.description: Topological pair density waves offer an insight into the interplay among finite-momentum pairing, topological matter and chiral superconductivity. This Perspective explores signatures of these states in kagome superconductors.

records.title: The post-quantum transition is a problem of coordination not of cryptography
records.description: Despite existing standards for quantum-safe encryption and regulatory deadlines, post-quantum migration is slow. The bottleneck is no longer mathematics or physics but collective action, but only the physics community can provide credible, calibrated estimates of when quantum computers will matter.

records.title: van der Waals Josephson junctions for quantum science and technology
records.description: van der Waals Josephson junctions offer opportunities to explore novel device functionalities in superconducting circuits. This Review discusses progress in different device architectures and provides a roadmap outlining near-term and long-term opportunities for the field.

records.title: What’s wrong with this intuition
records.description: This month, we reflect on the role of intuition — both physical and mathematical — in furthering our understanding of physics.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for representing and characterizing quantum systems
records.description: The application of artificial intelligence to quantum information science has emerged as a frontier of research. This Technical Review summarizes how AI techniques, including machine learning, deep learning and language models, are establishing a new way to describe complex quantum systems.

records.title: The work that holds physics together
records.description: In 1834, Mary Somerville’s On the Connexion of the Physical Sciences argued that astronomy, physics and mathematics belonged together. Saad Bhamla asks why this kind of synthesis tends to disappear into the subjects it organizes.

records.title: Drifting in the intestinal stem cell niche
records.description: Linus Chang explains how a paper that used statistical physics to explain how intestinal stem cells divide inspired his own work in biophysics.

records.title: The importance of imagery in quantum mechanics
records.description: 100 years on from Werner Heisenberg and Erwin Schrödinger’s dispute on how to conceptualize quantum mechanics, Arthur I. Miller reflects on the subtleties of visualization in physics.

records.title: Was Schrödinger ever a determinist?
records.description: Erwin Schrödinger is often portrayed as a reactionary who resisted the indeterminism introduced by quantum mechanics, but on closer inspection his views on determinism prove to be more complex and more radical.

records.title: Universal bounds on entropy production from fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories
records.description: Entropy production quantifies non-equilibrium behaviour but is hard to measure in fluctuating, partially observed systems. This Review discusses stochastic thermodynamics approaches that infer model-free lower bounds from coarse-grained observables, including states, currents, correlations and waiting times, across steady and time-dependent regimes, and highlights progress in trajectory-level estimation.

records.title: Emergence of Fermi-liquid and BCS physics in overdoped cuprates
records.description: Various observed behaviours of overdoped cuprates are inconsistent with a weak-coupling, Fermi-liquid-based Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer description. This Perspective argues that these behaviours are consequences of substitutional disorder in a d -wave superconductor with a short-correlation length, and that a weak-coupling approach is possible in the disorder-free limit.

records.title: Universities need transparent quantum hardware
records.description: Students need to experience quantum hardware beyond cloud access to learn how an ideal circuit becomes a physical measurement. Universities should therefore procure teachable systems, not showroom machines.

records.title: Graphene FET microfluidic platform for electrochemical molecular fingerprinting
records.description: Roanne Aves describes a platform to integrate graphene-FET based microfluidic modules into one experimental workflow.

records.title: Complexity from minimal state spreading
records.description: Rathindra Nath Das recounts how a simple framework to assess complexity published in 2022 shaped his own approach to physics.

records.title: Non-idealities in artificial synapses
records.description: Artificial synapses based on non-volatile memory exhibit non-ideal effects that can limit the performance of neuromorphic systems. This Review discusses their origins, mitigation strategies and opportunities to exploit these non-idealities for new computing functionalities.

records.title: The unreasonable usefulness of black holes
records.description: Ubiquitous in popular culture, black holes were once highly debated and remain an intellectually active research area with applications in volcano monitoring and bone growth.

records.title: Ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy
records.description: Terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy integrates picosecond pulses with atomic resolution, enabling detailed analysis of electron dynamics and molecular motions. This Technical Review outlines methods and applications, emphasizing insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials and technologies.

records.title: Discovery is not the opposite of application
records.description: Restructuring research funding as a choice between discovery and application gets the economics wrong, the evidence wrong and the people wrong.

records.title: Data-driven discovery of dynamical models in biology
records.description: This Technical Review compares data-driven approaches for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression-based methods, network-based architectures and decomposition techniques. It describes how these approaches extract dynamical information from time-resolved data and evaluates their strengths, limitations and complementarity.

records.title: Radioactive molecules as laboratories of fundamental physics
records.description: Radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei offer a promising platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations and searching for new physics. This Perspective discusses how advances in their production, trapping and molecular quantum control are enabling precision tests of fundamental physics at energy scales complementary to those probed by high-energy colliders.

records.title: Electrospray ion beam deposition for scanning tunnelling microscopy of complex molecules
records.description: Dhaneesh Kumar describes a method to enable the surface imaging of complex molecules.

records.title: Forty years of atomic force microscopy
records.description: Atomic force microscopy (AFM), first published in 1986, is now a workhorse of laboratories in physics and beyond. In this Viewpoint, seven scientists describe the variety of ways they use the technique and discuss how they’d like to see it develop in the future.

records.title: The physics of GaN-based light-emitting diodes
records.description: Because gallium nitride light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have made most of the visible spectrum available to LEDs, they have become the backbone of modern lighting applications. This Review examines three effects governing the physics of GaN-based LEDs: polarization fields, carrier localization and non-radiative defects.

records.title: How to probe lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy
records.description: Furqanul Hassan Naqvi explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy can provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.

records.title: The costs and benefits of physics research
records.description: Deciding what physics research to pursue involves cost–benefit analysis — which should include environmental impacts.

records.title: Atomic force microscopy from nanoscale imaging to holistic exploration
records.description: Forty years after its invention, atomic force microscopy has evolved from a simple surface imaging tool into one of the most versatile measurement platforms in nanoscience. This Comment traces the key innovations.

records.title: Exploring decolonizing the curriculum using Six Thinking Hats
records.description: Decolonizing physics is a scientific necessity often stalled by ‘competence anxiety’. By using the Six Thinking Hats framework, educators can navigate these challenging conversations with structure and safety.

records.title: How to probe lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy
records.description: Furqanul Hassan Naqvi explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy can provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.

records.title: The costs and benefits of physics research
records.description: Deciding what physics research to pursue involves cost–benefit analysis — which should include environmental impacts.

records.title: Atomic force microscopy from nanoscale imaging to holistic exploration
records.description: Forty years after its invention, atomic force microscopy has evolved from a simple surface imaging tool into one of the most versatile measurement platforms in nanoscience. This Comment traces the key innovations.

records.title: Exploring decolonizing the curriculum using Six Thinking Hats
records.description: Decolonizing physics is a scientific necessity often stalled by ‘competence anxiety’. By using the Six Thinking Hats framework, educators can navigate these challenging conversations with structure and safety.

records.title: Do the benefits of fundamental physics research outweigh its wider societal costs?
records.description: Deciding whether a big science project is sustainable is a complex multi-dimensional problem, but there are tools from economics that can help with decision making.

records.title: Transparent conducting electrodes for perovskite–silicon tandem solar cells
records.description: Transparent conducting electrodes are a key performance and sustainability bottleneck in high-efficiency perovskite–silicon tandem solar cells. This Review examines how optical, electrical and interfacial losses in transparent conducting electrodes arise in tandem cells and outlines strategies to enable scalable, low-indium electrodes for next-generation devices.

records.title: Transitions of the Atlantic Ocean circulation
records.description: The multistable dynamics of the Atlantic Ocean circulation pose a central problem in climate physics, because instabilities of the flows can have large climate impacts. This Review uses a dynamical systems viewpoint to unify results obtained from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models.

records.title: Chaotic photonics in microresonators
records.description: Chaos in photonics is not always a nuisance but often a source of innovation. This Review surveys chaotic microcavity photonics across materials and architectures, highlighting opportunities to harness chaotic dynamics for technology and science.

records.title: Cross-probing van der Waals multiferroics
records.description: 2D van der Waals multiferroics, with their coupled magnetic and electric orders and their reduced dimensionality, offer great opportunities for low-power magnetoelectric devices. This Review moves beyond conventional probing techniques and advocates for cross-probing technologies to identify intrinsic multiferroicity in these atomically thin materials.

records.title: Vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates
records.description: Polaritons can be optically driven into nonlinear states such as vortices and solitons, with properties like quantized phase jumps and stable shapes, that enable applications in information processing. This Review discusses the formation and control of polariton vortices and solitons.

records.title: Talking quantum with a 9-year-old
records.description: Katia Moskvitch shares her experience of launching a quantum computing podcast with her child.

records.title: Learning density functionals with differentiable DFT
records.description: Antonius von Strachwitz explains the advantages and challenges of replacing the exchange-correlation functionals in DFT with a learnable model.

records.title: Global science in a changing world
records.description: A closer look at past and present shows how trust underpins the international scientific endeavour.

records.title: Black-hole thermodynamics
records.description: The study of black-hole thermodynamics — now 50 years old — has led to deep insights into fundamental physics, but it has also created fresh paradoxes and puzzles. This Review assesses what has been learned, where progress is being made, and what remains unknown.

records.title: Physics and chemistry perspectives on three unsolved problems in glass science
records.description: This Perspective reviews recent progress in relation to three old yet unsolved problems on supercooled liquids and glasses, emphasizing the different approach and focus of physics and chemistry.

records.title: Interpreting coherence in wall turbulence
records.description: Although no universally accepted definition exists, coherent structures are key organized features of wall-bounded turbulent flows. This Review clarifies competing CS interpretations and highlights challenges in establishing causal relationships among CSs and in their interpretation via machine learning.

records.title: Reconfigurable and programmable integrated topological photonics
records.description: Topological photonic chips can be controlled globally, across the lattice, and locally, at the level of individual sites. This Review discusses these programmable and reconfigurable technologies for topological, quantum and non-Hermitian physics.

records.title: Material insights on electronic transport of charge and heat from first principles
records.description: Recent advances in first-principles computation are enabling quantitative predictions of electronic transport properties in materials. This Review explores the material insights and chemical intuition these advances offer and highlights prospects for discovering new materials across a broader spectrum.

records.title: Political isolationism can drive domestic capability but undermines global scientific progress
records.description: As the USA cuts research ties with China, historian Dazhou Wang looks back at a similar scientific rupture in the 1960s and argues that although China was able to make progress despite its isolation, collaboration remains better for science.

records.title: Realization of 2D metals and emergent quantum phenomena
records.description: 2D materials are appealing for emergent phenomena and applications, but despite the realization of many 2D layered crystals, 2D metals remain hard to realize because of their non-layered nature. In the past year, a van der Waals squeezing method has been developed for the production of diverse 2D metals at ångström-scale thickness, revealing exceptional quantum transport.

records.title: Experimental measurements of the quantum metric
records.description: Global topological invariants are a useful tool to understand electronic structure, but to understand emergent quantum phenomena, the local geometric structure of Bloch wavefunctions must be considered. In 2025, experiments have revealed the direct momentum-resolved measurement of the complete quantum metric tensor, enabling the experimental exploration of quantum geometry.

records.title: Quantum geometry and the hidden scales in materials
records.description: Quantum geometry captures how electronic wavefunctions delocalize across crystal lattices, introducing length and energy scales beyond band dispersion. This Perspective shows how these hidden scales shape material properties, from dielectric response and optical absorption to the robustness of superconductivity and other emergent phases.

records.title: Sub-diffraction confinement in dielectrics with narwhal wavefunctions
records.description: Overcoming the diffraction limit in lossless dielectrics has long been thought impossible. This Perspective explores how the narwhal wavefunction enables lossless, deep-subwavelength optical confinement, offering a new framework for dielectric nanophotonics.

records.title: Physics of sphere packings
records.description: Sphere packings provide deep physical insights about the structural and bulk physical properties of condensed phases of matter. This Review surveys recent theoretical progress on the study of disordered and ordered frictionless identical hard spheres.

records.title: Serendipity in an algorithm-driven culture
records.description: Algorithmic tools promise to help researchers cut through the mass of scientific literature, but serendipitous encounters with papers remain essential for scientific progress.

records.title: Upconverting nanoparticles for biomedical applications
records.description: Lanthanide-doped upconverting nanoparticles enable nonlinear anti-Stokes light conversion, which has shown unique photophysics and cross-disciplinary, particularly biomedical, applications. This Review covers mechanisms, uses and field-shaping challenges and chances.

records.title: Carrier transport in emerging 2D materials
records.description: Kunal Tiwari explains how a 2022 paper on THz spectroscopy on MXenes inspired him to step out of his comfort zone and explore a new research topic.

records.title: Size-controlled growth of anisotropic gold nanoparticles
records.description: Tomohiro Nobeyama remembers how a 2014 paper taught him about nanoparticle synthesis and how to write a good research article.

records.title: Metrics for spin-based computing
records.description: A number of different platforms for spin-based computing have emerged over the past few years, offering energy-efficient computing methods. This Technical Review identifies key metrics that must be evaluated to benchmark their performance.

records.title: Simulating fermions with a digital quantum computer
records.description: To simulate physical systems on a quantum computer, their degrees of freedom must be encoded into qubits. This Review assesses the different methods that exist to allow quantum calculation of fermionic systems.

records.title: Collective dynamics on higher-order networks
records.description: This Review surveys how higher-order interactions, which link more than two units at a time, reshape collective dynamics in complex systems. New synchronization phenomena, analytical frameworks and emerging methods to reduce or infer higher-order structure from data, are highlighted.

records.title: Writing in the age of chatbots
records.description: As chatbots become more ubiquitous in our everyday lives, we remind our readers that good writing comes from knowing what you want to say.

records.title: Terahertz 2D coherent spectroscopy for probing and controlling multicorrelations in quantum matter
records.description: Terahertz 2D coherent spectroscopy can be used to probe phase-resolved, multidimensional spectra of quantum materials. This Perspective discusses the capabilities of this method and provides a comparison with other multidimensional spectroscopies.

records.title: Simulating topological order on quantum processors
records.description: Topological phases in quantum many-body systems emerge from long-range entanglement rather than symmetry breaking, giving rise to properties such as topology-dependent degeneracy, protected edge modes and anyonic excitations. This Review discusses recent advances on how to realize and study such interacting topological states on digital quantum computers.

records.title: Bottom-up mesoscopic coarse-graining of soft matter
Publisher Correction: Warm dense matter studies with X-ray free-electron lasers
The Yang–Mills Millennium problem
records.description: Yang–Mills theory is the basis of the standard model of particle physics. The Yang–Mills Millennium Prize problem, to show that the theory is mathematically well defined and that it has the mass gap property, is one of the great challenges of mathematical physics. This Review explores the problem from both physical and mathematical points of view and surveys promising approaches from recent years.

records.title: Opportunities and challenges of quantum batteries
records.description: Quantum batteries are miniaturized energy storage devices that exploit the laws of quantum mechanics. This Perspective highlights major theoretical and experimental advances, promising directions and key challenges in this emerging field.

records.title: Let’s talk about limitations
records.description: Review articles often celebrate the wins of a research field, but they can also play a crucial role in highlighting limitations to bring realistic opportunities into focus.

records.title: Inside the International Asteroid Warning Network
records.description: Kelly Fast, Acting Planetary Defense Officer for NASA, describes the global network working to detect and assess asteroids that could potentially threaten Earth.

It distinguishes engineering, statistical, thermodynamic and ontological faces of information, each with distinctive affordances and restrictions.

records.title: Topological pair density waves in kagome superconductors
records.description: Topological pair density waves offer an insight into the interplay among finite-momentum pairing, topological matter and chiral superconductivity. This Perspective explores signatures of these states in kagome superconductors.

records.title: The post-quantum transition is a problem of coordination not of cryptography
records.description: Despite existing standards for quantum-safe encryption and regulatory deadlines, post-quantum migration is slow. The bottleneck is no longer mathematics or physics but collective action, but only the physics community can provide credible, calibrated estimates of when quantum computers will matter.

records.title: van der Waals Josephson junctions for quantum science and technology
records.description: van der Waals Josephson junctions offer opportunities to explore novel device functionalities in superconducting circuits. This Review discusses progress in different device architectures and provides a roadmap outlining near-term and long-term opportunities for the field.

records.title: What’s wrong with this intuition
records.description: This month, we reflect on the role of intuition — both physical and mathematical — in furthering our understanding of physics.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for representing and characterizing quantum systems
records.description: The application of artificial intelligence to quantum information science has emerged as a frontier of research. This Technical Review summarizes how AI techniques, including machine learning, deep learning and language models, are establishing a new way to describe complex quantum systems.

records.title: The work that holds physics together
records.description: In 1834, Mary Somerville’s On the Connexion of the Physical Sciences argued that astronomy, physics and mathematics belonged together. Saad Bhamla asks why this kind of synthesis tends to disappear into the subjects it organizes.

records.title: Drifting in the intestinal stem cell niche
records.description: Linus Chang explains how a paper that used statistical physics to explain how intestinal stem cells divide inspired his own work in biophysics.

records.title: The importance of imagery in quantum mechanics
records.description: 100 years on from Werner Heisenberg and Erwin Schrödinger’s dispute on how to conceptualize quantum mechanics, Arthur I. Miller reflects on the subtleties of visualization in physics.

records.title: Was Schrödinger ever a determinist?
records.description: Erwin Schrödinger is often portrayed as a reactionary who resisted the indeterminism introduced by quantum mechanics, but on closer inspection his views on determinism prove to be more complex and more radical.

records.title: Universal bounds on entropy production from fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories
records.description: Entropy production quantifies non-equilibrium behaviour but is hard to measure in fluctuating, partially observed systems. This Review discusses stochastic thermodynamics approaches that infer model-free lower bounds from coarse-grained observables, including states, currents, correlations and waiting times, across steady and time-dependent regimes, and highlights progress in trajectory-level estimation.

records.title: Emergence of Fermi-liquid and BCS physics in overdoped cuprates
records.description: Various observed behaviours of overdoped cuprates are inconsistent with a weak-coupling, Fermi-liquid-based Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer description. This Perspective argues that these behaviours are consequences of substitutional disorder in a d -wave superconductor with a short-correlation length, and that a weak-coupling approach is possible in the disorder-free limit.

records.title: Universities need transparent quantum hardware
records.description: Students need to experience quantum hardware beyond cloud access to learn how an ideal circuit becomes a physical measurement. Universities should therefore procure teachable systems, not showroom machines.

records.title: Graphene FET microfluidic platform for electrochemical molecular fingerprinting
records.description: Roanne Aves describes a platform to integrate graphene-FET based microfluidic modules into one experimental workflow.

records.title: Complexity from minimal state spreading
records.description: Rathindra Nath Das recounts how a simple framework to assess complexity published in 2022 shaped his own approach to physics.

records.title: Non-idealities in artificial synapses
records.description: Artificial synapses based on non-volatile memory exhibit non-ideal effects that can limit the performance of neuromorphic systems. This Review discusses their origins, mitigation strategies and opportunities to exploit these non-idealities for new computing functionalities.

records.title: The unreasonable usefulness of black holes
records.description: Ubiquitous in popular culture, black holes were once highly debated and remain an intellectually active research area with applications in volcano monitoring and bone growth.

records.title: Ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy
records.description: Terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy integrates picosecond pulses with atomic resolution, enabling detailed analysis of electron dynamics and molecular motions. This Technical Review outlines methods and applications, emphasizing insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials and technologies.

records.title: Discovery is not the opposite of application
records.description: Restructuring research funding as a choice between discovery and application gets the economics wrong, the evidence wrong and the people wrong.

records.title: Data-driven discovery of dynamical models in biology
records.description: This Technical Review compares data-driven approaches for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression-based methods, network-based architectures and decomposition techniques. It describes how these approaches extract dynamical information from time-resolved data and evaluates their strengths, limitations and complementarity.

records.title: Radioactive molecules as laboratories of fundamental physics
records.description: Radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei offer a promising platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations and searching for new physics. This Perspective discusses how advances in their production, trapping and molecular quantum control are enabling precision tests of fundamental physics at energy scales complementary to those probed by high-energy colliders.

records.title: Electrospray ion beam deposition for scanning tunnelling microscopy of complex molecules
records.description: Dhaneesh Kumar describes a method to enable the surface imaging of complex molecules.

records.title: Forty years of atomic force microscopy
records.description: Atomic force microscopy (AFM), first published in 1986, is now a workhorse of laboratories in physics and beyond. In this Viewpoint, seven scientists describe the variety of ways they use the technique and discuss how they’d like to see it develop in the future.

records.title: The physics of GaN-based light-emitting diodes
records.description: Because gallium nitride light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have made most of the visible spectrum available to LEDs, they have become the backbone of modern lighting applications. This Review examines three effects governing the physics of GaN-based LEDs: polarization fields, carrier localization and non-radiative defects.

records.title: How to probe lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy
records.description: Furqanul Hassan Naqvi explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy can provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.

records.title: The costs and benefits of physics research
records.description: Deciding what physics research to pursue involves cost–benefit analysis — which should include environmental impacts.

records.title: Atomic force microscopy from nanoscale imaging to holistic exploration
records.description: Forty years after its invention, atomic force microscopy has evolved from a simple surface imaging tool into one of the most versatile measurement platforms in nanoscience. This Comment traces the key innovations.

records.title: Exploring decolonizing the curriculum using Six Thinking Hats
records.description: Decolonizing physics is a scientific necessity often stalled by ‘competence anxiety’. By using the Six Thinking Hats framework, educators can navigate these challenging conversations with structure and safety.

records.title: How to probe lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy
records.description: Furqanul Hassan Naqvi explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy can provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.

records.title: The costs and benefits of physics research
records.description: Deciding what physics research to pursue involves cost–benefit analysis — which should include environmental impacts.

records.title: Atomic force microscopy from nanoscale imaging to holistic exploration
records.description: Forty years after its invention, atomic force microscopy has evolved from a simple surface imaging tool into one of the most versatile measurement platforms in nanoscience. This Comment traces the key innovations.

records.title: Exploring decolonizing the curriculum using Six Thinking Hats
records.description: Decolonizing physics is a scientific necessity often stalled by ‘competence anxiety’. By using the Six Thinking Hats framework, educators can navigate these challenging conversations with structure and safety.

records.title: Do the benefits of fundamental physics research outweigh its wider societal costs?
records.description: Deciding whether a big science project is sustainable is a complex multi-dimensional problem, but there are tools from economics that can help with decision making.

records.title: Transparent conducting electrodes for perovskite–silicon tandem solar cells
records.description: Transparent conducting electrodes are a key performance and sustainability bottleneck in high-efficiency perovskite–silicon tandem solar cells. This Review examines how optical, electrical and interfacial losses in transparent conducting electrodes arise in tandem cells and outlines strategies to enable scalable, low-indium electrodes for next-generation devices.

records.title: Transitions of the Atlantic Ocean circulation
records.description: The multistable dynamics of the Atlantic Ocean circulation pose a central problem in climate physics, because instabilities of the flows can have large climate impacts. This Review uses a dynamical systems viewpoint to unify results obtained from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models.

records.title: Chaotic photonics in microresonators
records.description: Chaos in photonics is not always a nuisance but often a source of innovation. This Review surveys chaotic microcavity photonics across materials and architectures, highlighting opportunities to harness chaotic dynamics for technology and science.

records.title: Cross-probing van der Waals multiferroics
records.description: 2D van der Waals multiferroics, with their coupled magnetic and electric orders and their reduced dimensionality, offer great opportunities for low-power magnetoelectric devices. This Review moves beyond conventional probing techniques and advocates for cross-probing technologies to identify intrinsic multiferroicity in these atomically thin materials.

records.title: Vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates
records.description: Polaritons can be optically driven into nonlinear states such as vortices and solitons, with properties like quantized phase jumps and stable shapes, that enable applications in information processing. This Review discusses the formation and control of polariton vortices and solitons.

records.title: Talking quantum with a 9-year-old
records.description: Katia Moskvitch shares her experience of launching a quantum computing podcast with her child.

records.title: Learning density functionals with differentiable DFT
records.description: Antonius von Strachwitz explains the advantages and challenges of replacing the exchange-correlation functionals in DFT with a learnable model.

records.title: Global science in a changing world
records.description: A closer look at past and present shows how trust underpins the international scientific endeavour.

records.title: Black-hole thermodynamics
records.description: The study of black-hole thermodynamics — now 50 years old — has led to deep insights into fundamental physics, but it has also created fresh paradoxes and puzzles. This Review assesses what has been learned, where progress is being made, and what remains unknown.

records.title: Physics and chemistry perspectives on three unsolved problems in glass science
records.description: This Perspective reviews recent progress in relation to three old yet unsolved problems on supercooled liquids and glasses, emphasizing the different approach and focus of physics and chemistry.

records.title: Interpreting coherence in wall turbulence
records.description: Although no universally accepted definition exists, coherent structures are key organized features of wall-bounded turbulent flows. This Review clarifies competing CS interpretations and highlights challenges in establishing causal relationships among CSs and in their interpretation via machine learning.

records.title: Reconfigurable and programmable integrated topological photonics
records.description: Topological photonic chips can be controlled globally, across the lattice, and locally, at the level of individual sites. This Review discusses these programmable and reconfigurable technologies for topological, quantum and non-Hermitian physics.

records.title: Material insights on electronic transport of charge and heat from first principles
records.description: Recent advances in first-principles computation are enabling quantitative predictions of electronic transport properties in materials. This Review explores the material insights and chemical intuition these advances offer and highlights prospects for discovering new materials across a broader spectrum.

records.title: Political isolationism can drive domestic capability but undermines global scientific progress
records.description: As the USA cuts research ties with China, historian Dazhou Wang looks back at a similar scientific rupture in the 1960s and argues that although China was able to make progress despite its isolation, collaboration remains better for science.

records.title: Realization of 2D metals and emergent quantum phenomena
records.description: 2D materials are appealing for emergent phenomena and applications, but despite the realization of many 2D layered crystals, 2D metals remain hard to realize because of their non-layered nature. In the past year, a van der Waals squeezing method has been developed for the production of diverse 2D metals at ångström-scale thickness, revealing exceptional quantum transport.

records.title: Experimental measurements of the quantum metric
records.description: Global topological invariants are a useful tool to understand electronic structure, but to understand emergent quantum phenomena, the local geometric structure of Bloch wavefunctions must be considered. In 2025, experiments have revealed the direct momentum-resolved measurement of the complete quantum metric tensor, enabling the experimental exploration of quantum geometry.

records.title: Quantum geometry and the hidden scales in materials
records.description: Quantum geometry captures how electronic wavefunctions delocalize across crystal lattices, introducing length and energy scales beyond band dispersion. This Perspective shows how these hidden scales shape material properties, from dielectric response and optical absorption to the robustness of superconductivity and other emergent phases.

records.title: Sub-diffraction confinement in dielectrics with narwhal wavefunctions
records.description: Overcoming the diffraction limit in lossless dielectrics has long been thought impossible. This Perspective explores how the narwhal wavefunction enables lossless, deep-subwavelength optical confinement, offering a new framework for dielectric nanophotonics.

records.title: Physics of sphere packings
records.description: Sphere packings provide deep physical insights about the structural and bulk physical properties of condensed phases of matter. This Review surveys recent theoretical progress on the study of disordered and ordered frictionless identical hard spheres.

records.title: Serendipity in an algorithm-driven culture
records.description: Algorithmic tools promise to help researchers cut through the mass of scientific literature, but serendipitous encounters with papers remain essential for scientific progress.

records.title: Upconverting nanoparticles for biomedical applications
records.description: Lanthanide-doped upconverting nanoparticles enable nonlinear anti-Stokes light conversion, which has shown unique photophysics and cross-disciplinary, particularly biomedical, applications. This Review covers mechanisms, uses and field-shaping challenges and chances.

records.title: Carrier transport in emerging 2D materials
records.description: Kunal Tiwari explains how a 2022 paper on THz spectroscopy on MXenes inspired him to step out of his comfort zone and explore a new research topic.

records.title: Size-controlled growth of anisotropic gold nanoparticles
records.description: Tomohiro Nobeyama remembers how a 2014 paper taught him about nanoparticle synthesis and how to write a good research article.

records.title: Metrics for spin-based computing
records.description: A number of different platforms for spin-based computing have emerged over the past few years, offering energy-efficient computing methods. This Technical Review identifies key metrics that must be evaluated to benchmark their performance.

records.title: Simulating fermions with a digital quantum computer
records.description: To simulate physical systems on a quantum computer, their degrees of freedom must be encoded into qubits. This Review assesses the different methods that exist to allow quantum calculation of fermionic systems.

records.title: Collective dynamics on higher-order networks
records.description: This Review surveys how higher-order interactions, which link more than two units at a time, reshape collective dynamics in complex systems. New synchronization phenomena, analytical frameworks and emerging methods to reduce or infer higher-order structure from data, are highlighted.

records.title: Writing in the age of chatbots
records.description: As chatbots become more ubiquitous in our everyday lives, we remind our readers that good writing comes from knowing what you want to say.

records.title: Terahertz 2D coherent spectroscopy for probing and controlling multicorrelations in quantum matter
records.description: Terahertz 2D coherent spectroscopy can be used to probe phase-resolved, multidimensional spectra of quantum materials. This Perspective discusses the capabilities of this method and provides a comparison with other multidimensional spectroscopies.

records.title: Simulating topological order on quantum processors
records.description: Topological phases in quantum many-body systems emerge from long-range entanglement rather than symmetry breaking, giving rise to properties such as topology-dependent degeneracy, protected edge modes and anyonic excitations. This Review discusses recent advances on how to realize and study such interacting topological states on digital quantum computers.

records.title: Bottom-up mesoscopic coarse-graining of soft matter
Publisher Correction: Warm dense matter studies with X-ray free-electron lasers
The Yang–Mills Millennium problem
records.description: Yang–Mills theory is the basis of the standard model of particle physics. The Yang–Mills Millennium Prize problem, to show that the theory is mathematically well defined and that it has the mass gap property, is one of the great challenges of mathematical physics. This Review explores the problem from both physical and mathematical points of view and surveys promising approaches from recent years.

records.title: Opportunities and challenges of quantum batteries
records.description: Quantum batteries are miniaturized energy storage devices that exploit the laws of quantum mechanics. This Perspective highlights major theoretical and experimental advances, promising directions and key challenges in this emerging field.

records.title: Let’s talk about limitations
records.description: Review articles often celebrate the wins of a research field, but they can also play a crucial role in highlighting limitations to bring realistic opportunities into focus.

records.title: Inside the International Asteroid Warning Network
records.description: Kelly Fast, Acting Planetary Defense Officer for NASA, describes the global network working to detect and assess asteroids that could potentially threaten Earth.
